claims.statement: MDS_DATA position 139 (SUBSTRING("MDS_DATA" FROM 139 FOR 1), 1-based) is the process-loop flag: 0=normal mainline, 1=quality rework, 2=blacktop second spray, -=unfilled (value 3 occurs in only 4 anomalous rows); it operates as a body real-time state machine (decision made mid-production, bit flips only after), so the latest event's flag equals the current state and flag=0 covers both 'never reworked' and 'rework completed, back on mainline'.

MDS_DATA position 137 (SUBSTRING("MDS_DATA" FROM 137 FOR 1)) is the black-roof (two-tone) configuration flag, essentially lifetime-invariant (real changes observed on only 4 vehicles), and it is a hard precondition for accepting any 139=2 blacktop anchor (docs/15 C3).

The raw 139 bit is sticky after loop exit: 86.62% of the 14,078 exited rework vehicles (docs/13 §2.3) still carried 139=1 at the final telegram at the 4 exit read stations, and the full-window measurement behind docs/14 v1.4 found the raw bit uncleared for 96% of rework cars and 45% of blacktop cars after loop exit; therefore 139='0' must not be used as the loop-exit criterion, which motivates both the offline purification windows and the online loop-exit guard (R3'/R2.4).

97.17% of the first 139=1 events of the 14,354 rework vehicles concentrate at the three sanding-prep stations 15IS065 (47.81%) / 13IS065 (27.64%) / 14IS065 (21.72%); before these stations (pre-treatment, electrocoat, sealing, pre-spray sanding) the bit is 100% '0', making them the physical Loop-1 inbound anchors.

The physical rework loop-exit anchor is the three-line handover gateway group {25IS010, 25IS110, 25IS210} (first pass after tagging): coverage 98.17% (14,092 cars) per docs/13 §2.4 and the unified full-history caliber 97.99% (14,065 cars) per docs/14; the previous single-25IS110 anchor silently dropped 1,889 rework cars (13.13%), 1,870 of them finished cars exiting via line 1 / alternative routes, biasing training samples toward lines 2/3.

At the line-2 main gateway 25IS110 the median remaining time to the final exit point for flag=0 cars (P50 1.95h, 67,260 cars) and flag=1 cars (P50 1.98h, 11,638 cars) differs by only 2.1 minutes, proving that crossing the gateway fully exits the rework loop and downstream behavior is physically equivalent to normal cars (line-1 25IS010 shows 2.42h vs 3.50h with ~1h lateral queue confirmation at 25IS365; line-3 25IS210 3.28h).

The naive span MAX(t)-MIN(t) WHERE flag=1 (P50 17.99h / mean 38.99h) counts the post-loop waxing corridor and exit waiting into the loop; the true physical span (first sanding tag to first gateway-group pass) is P50 13.60h / mean 28.23h, a systematic inflation of +4.39h (+32.3%) at P50 and +10.77h (+38.2%) at the mean removed by the dual-anchor closure.

The three parallel topcoat bake-oven exit stations 16IS305 (line 1) / 17IS305 (line 2) / 18IS345 (line 3) are the hard physical threshold for blacktop second-spray anchoring: the base coat must cross-link and cool at an oven exit before masking and black roof re-spray is physically possible, so any 139=2 before the first oven-exit pass is a false signal (28 victim-group cars as exception); strict post-oven-exit anchoring compresses residual bias to under 0.5%.

4,941 single-tone cars (137=0, G0) show a transient 139=2 scheduling signal while queuing at the first-spray entry 14IS260/13IS260 (median duration 4.8 min, 100% reset within the spray-queue segment, at most 2 events per car); the naive MIN-based extraction produced a physically meaningless P50=4.9h phantom peak in the ALL flag2 row of dss.dim_loop_duration, so every blacktop anchor must require SUBSTRING("MDS_DATA" FROM 137 FOR 1) = '1'.

536 blacktop cars (9.1% of the 5,877-car G1 group; plus 45 on 13IS260, 581 total) have their first 139=2 on the 14IS260 spray queue (two-phase flash 3.7 min, reset 0, then formal second-spray tag); naive loop-start treatment inflated the victim group by +3.38h median / +9.28h mean (long tail to 203.8h); under the corrected 137=1 and post-oven-exit anchor first tags converge to the report-entry cluster (88.1%) plus sanding-rework lines (10.8%), 99.0% physical placement, 98.9% coverage (5,813/5,877), eliminating all 488 truly contaminated cars.

The clean-suffix backward method (Plan B) has a 5.3% structural failure: 112 cars (1.9%) read a 0 reset at post-exit 09IS360 with no events after the last non-2 (NULL anchors) and 199 cars (3.4%) took 139=1 rework inside the loop, breaking the trailing 2 and causing systematic 16.16h underestimation; it is demoted from training main anchor to fallback for the 8 cars without oven events plus an offline cross-check.

spike_w1/sqlbase.py::ev_base_sql derives per-vehicle dual-loop windows in tmp_loop_bounds: t_rw_start = first raw 139=1; t_bt_start = first event with flag_137='1' AND raw 139=2 at or after the first oven-out over the errata 3-station set {16IS305,17IS305,18IS345}; t_rw_end/t_bt_end = first pass of {25IS010,25IS110,25IS210} after tagging (NULL = no gateway); tmp_ev_base.flag is purified to '1' inside [t_rw_start,t_rw_end] (priority), '2' inside [t_bt_start,t_bt_end], and '0' for everything else (post-gateway, pre-oven false signals, -/3 invalid values), with last_loop_t = max(t) FILTER (WHERE flag IN ('1','2')) OVER (PARTITION BY body) byte-for-byte unchanged, preserving the clean-suffix exclusion.

C5 dual-window truncation (docs/14 v1.3 D14-1; docs/15 C5): for rework-first handover cars (t_bt_start > t_rw_start) the rework window upper bound is LEAST(first gateway, t_bt_start); without it the blacktop segment [bt_start, gateway] (17,457 events, 5.66% of all '1'-flagged events, P50 6.35h / mean 15.00h) would be mislabeled '1' and inflate rework L1 by +8.46h (P50); after truncation the rework segment recovers to true P50 3.74h / mean 11.88h and the blacktop segment falls into the '2' branch; the 158 blacktop-first handover cars are unaffected and the 864 false-signal cars are purified to '0'.

The oven-out station set was erratum-corrected from 4 stations to 3: 20IS010 is the line-2 bake-oven storage-line entry (median 46s after 17IS305), not an oven exit, and measured zero car-passes at 20IS010 earlier than the three exits; shipped code (spike_w1/sqlbase.py first_oven, spike_w2/eta_v2.py OVEN_OUT_STATIONS) uses the corrected 3-station set {16IS305,17IS305,18IS345}, while docs/12 §3/§5.1 and the README 黑车顶大环线锚定 row still list the stale 4-station set — per the single-source-of-truth order the docs/15 erratum and shipped code prevail (以 BM 笔记为准).

resolve_effective_flag rule R1: if the current station is in UNIVERSAL_EXIT_STATIONS (37 stations: gateway trio, direct transfer, waxing/assembly corridor, exit corridor) the engine forces the effective flag to '0' with highest priority, ignoring resident telegram bits; after unfreezing, prediction must converge to the body-type-specific clean mainline baseline row with tiered fallback (e.g. IE14.- ~16.5h after the gateway), and a plant-wide pooled ~2h scalar is strictly forbidden (docs/15 C7).

Rule R2 for raw 139=2 applies four-fold protection: 2.1 137 != '1' (including missing '-') -> '0' (blocks the 4,941 G0 flash cars); 2.2 station in SPRAY_QUEUE_BLACKLIST (14IS260/13IS260) and passed_oven=False -> '0'; 2.3 passed_oven=False and station not in BLACKTOP_ONLINE_WHITELIST -> '0'; 2.4 (v1.4) loop_exited=True -> '0' (a past-gateway car has by construction already been oven-out, so the oven/whitelist defenses are pierced and the measured 45% residual '2' bit is frozen); otherwise the effective flag is '2'.

Rule R3': raw 139=1 resolves to '1' only when loop_exited=False (first-tag concentration at the sanding stations 97.17% per docs/13; the Doc14/code comment rounds it to 97.12%); when loop_exited=True the residual bit is frozen to '0', mirroring the offline purified-window semantics [first raw-1, 25IS exit] online; loop_exited defaults to False = old semantics, so the DSS_DUAL_RING=0 rollback path, the static effective_flag passthrough path, and existing unit tests are unaffected.

The W3 pool maintains two per-car signals: O1 passed_oven is monotone set-once (pre-seeded True if adoption happens at an oven-exit station; set True, never reset, when a pool event passes an OVEN_OUT_STATIONS station; slice-replay merge is monotone OR); O2 flag_137 follows the car as the latest event's 137-bit value, normalized with '-' treated as '0' and no cross-car contamination.

The pool's loop_exited (W4.4c (α), Doc14 v1.4): pre-seeded True if adoption happens at a LOOP_EXIT_GATEWAYS station {25IS010,25IS110,25IS210}; set True when a pool event is at any gateway station (mainline residual-bit events do not reset it — the bit not being cleared is a data fact); reset to False only on the new-cycle signal: an in-pool car passing an entry station again, which also resets entry_ts and loop_count; slice-replay merges 25IS-exit events to True and entry-station events to False (same walk order as _ingest_core), leaving the stored value untouched when the slice has no signal; invalid raw flags (3/-) inherit the last valid flag and never reset it to 0.

The dashboard single-car CLI mirrors loop_exited and passed_oven as stateless single SQL count queries (did this car reach the 25IS gateway exits / oven exits at or before as_of); the known simplification misjudges the rare 'second rework after loop exit' car as mainline (0 cars measured in the KW36/37 window), while the online rolling-pool path carries the full state.

estimate_event_unified branches on the effective flag: branch A (eff in {'1','2'}) takes rem from dss.dim_loop_remaining via three-tier hierarchical resolve (model, platform prefix LEFT(model,2), 'ALL', row n>=30), falls back to dss.dim_loop_duration L, returns (None, False) if all missing, and computes eta = t + round(rem) with no additive term (docs/15 C8: loop tables' training target is station-to-exit full journey); branch B (eff='0') takes the mainline base from line-cohort mixing or the rem table and adds the expected net delay from resolve_expected_delay (delay forced 0 when the station is in UNIVERSAL_EXIT_STATIONS); mode='shift' consumes mean columns and mode='vehicle' P50 (docs/15 C9), with alpha applied once at the consumption point, never inside the estimator.

The effective_flag passthrough channel (docs/15 blocking item 3) lets replay sides pass the already-purified tmp_ev_base flag directly, skipping the online state machine (offline purification is ground truth and the state machine is its stateless mirror); replay must not instead pass raw 137/139 + passed_oven, because a missing 137 bit would mis-kill all pure blacktop cars back to '0'; the online side (predictor.rem_of) always passes effective_flag=None and runs the full state machine with the pool's flag_137, passed_oven, and loop_exited.

Engine gates: DSS_DUAL_RING defaults to 1 (unified engine production default; 0 = legacy-path rollback; strict 1/0 parsing that raises on invalid values); DSS_USE_NET_DELAY is effective only under DUAL_RING=0 (doc10 retrofit replacing p*L compensation with expected_delay); DSS_SHIFT_TIER_DELAY=1 makes the unified delay prefer shift-tier rows (entry_shift DAY/MID) with fallback to shared rows, and 0 = zero drift; the legacy estimate_event path is retained unchanged for the rollback path and existing test anchors.

The dual-ring caliber is pinned by DB-free tests: tests/test_w4_eta_unified.py (physical constant sets verbatim + resolve_effective_flag case matrix incl. R1 priority and R2.4/R3' guards), tests/test_w4_loop_exit_guard.py (R3'/R2.4 suppression, unified branch-selection lock for exited vs default cars, pool loop_exited transitions incl. adoption pre-seed and slice merge, dashboard mainline behavior), tests/test_w4_sqlbase.py (SQL text: '78202%%' predicate, both 137/139 SUBSTRING extractions, errata 3-station oven set with explicit assertion that 20IS010 is absent, 3-station gateway set, C5 LEAST truncation, purified-flag CASE, unchanged last_loop_t and LAG dedup), and tests/test_w4_pipeline_flag137.py (O1/O2 pool contract).
